page.layout: One column of running text, set full width with the printed "»" line marks at the left edge of each line. Below the last line, at the right, the catchword "pro". Running head at the top. Page number 32 at the top left.

main_text.p: auctoritate necessariam esse difputationem fori. Hæc di-fputatio & hoc ius, quod fi-ne fcripto venit, compositũ à prudentibus, propria parte aliqua non appellatur, ut ce-terae partes iuris suis nominibus defignantur, datis proprijs nominibus ceteris partibus: sed cõmuni nomine appellatur ius ciuile. Quibus ex verbis intelligimus, quod singulari [?] animadverfione dignum est, tantam huiusce Iuris dignitatem præstatiamq; fuisse, ut commune Iuris ciuilis nomen suum ac proprium effecerit. cuius rei documenta sunt in oratione Ciceronis

page.notes: The "»" marks at the start of each line are printer's line ornaments, not text, and are left out. The running head is set in heavy decorative type and I could not read it. The word "fin gulari" is printed with a broken word at the line end and no hyphen, read as "singulari"; the first letters are doubtful. The catchword "pro" is at the foot and is not repeated in the text. Printed "compositũ" and "cõmuni" keep their tilde as printed.
